**1. Summary of the Paper Under Review:**
The paper "DiscQuant" proposes a novel approach to weight rounding in post-training quantization (PTQ) leveraging **discrepancy theory** (Lovett-Meka) and **gradient covariance assumptions**.
- **Core Contribution:** A theoretical bound (Theorem 3.3) proving low-rank gradient covariance allows rounding most weights with bounded error. This is contrasted with standard Hessian-based methods (GPTQ).
- **Algorithm:** "DiscQuant," a practical SGD-based method combining KL-divergence distillation with a linear regularizer derived from the theoretical insight.
- **Empirical Results:** Strong performance on Phi-3-mini and Llama-3.1-8B, consistently outperforming GPTQ and RTN, especially on GSM8k (e.g., 64% vs 54% at 3.25 bits).
- **Weaknesses:** Significant gap between the theoretical algorithm (Lovett-Meka) and practical optimization (SLD); questionable validation of the low-rank assumption due to JL projection on gradients; missing ablation on the linear regularizer's specific contribution; some under-specified hyperparameters.
